    MathOverflow = 1,

//! Per-handler guard checks derived from the `.qedspec`.
//! Called from user-owned `instructions/<name>::handler` before
//! business logic; keep guard logic here, policy-free logic there.

#![allow(
    unused_variables,
    unused_imports,
    dead_code,
    clippy::too_many_arguments
)]

use crate::errors::*;
use crate::math::*;
use crate::state::*;
use crate::*;
use anchor_lang::prelude::*;

/// Guards for `collect`.  
/// Generated from the `requires` clauses of the spec handler block.
pub fn collect<'info>(ctx: &mut Collect<'info>, total: u64) -> Result<()> {
    // let-binding from spec: fee = (mul_div_floor_u128(((total) as u128), ((s.fee_bps) as u128), ((10000) as u128))) as u64
    let fee = (mul_div_floor_u128(
        ((total) as u128),
        ((ctx.state.fee_bps) as u128),
        ((10000) as u128),
    )) as u64;
    // let-binding from spec: net = total - fee
    let net = total - fee;
    // requires: total > 0
    if !(total > 0) {
        return Err(FeeSplitError::DustAmount.into());
    }
    // requires: net > 0
    if !(net > 0) {
        return Err(FeeSplitError::DustAmount.into());
    }
    Ok(())
}

// ---- END GENERATED ----

--- src/instructions/collect.rs ---
// User-owned. Regenerating the spec does NOT overwrite this file.
// Guard checks live in the sibling `crate::guards` module and ARE
// regenerated on every `qedgen codegen`. Drift between the spec
// handler block and the `spec_hash` below fires a compile_error!
// via the `#[qed(verified, ...)]` macro.

use crate::errors::*;
use crate::guards;
use crate::Collect;
use anchor_lang::prelude::*;
use qedgen_macros::qed;

impl<'info> Collect<'info> {
    #[qed(
        verified,
        spec = "../fee_split.qedspec",
        handler = "collect",
        hash = "7cb36448f8bae251",
        spec_hash = "433797386f37f406"
    )]
    #[inline(always)]
    pub fn handler(&mut self, total: u64) -> Result<()> {
        guards::collect(self, total)?;
        let fee = (mul_div_floor_u128(
            ((total) as u128),
            ((self.state.fee_bps) as u128),
            ((10000) as u128),
        )) as u64;
        let net = total - fee;
        self.state.pool = self
            .state
            .pool
            .checked_add(net)
            .ok_or(FeeSplitError::MathOverflow)?;
        self.state.fees = self
            .state
            .fees
            .checked_add(fee)
            .ok_or(FeeSplitError::MathOverflow)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

    use super::*;

    pub fn collect(ctx: Context<Collect>, total: u64) -> Result<()> {
        ctx.accounts.handler(total)
    }
}

// `#[derive(Accounts)]` structs live at the crate root so the
// Anchor `#[program]` macro can resolve them via `crate::*`.
// The handler impl blocks live next to the (always-regenerated)
// guard module in `instructions/<name>.rs`.
use crate::state::*;

#[derive(Accounts)]
pub struct Collect<'info> {
    #[account(mut)]
    pub state: Account<'info, FeeSplitAccount>,
}

--- src/math.rs ---
// ---- GENERATED BY QEDGEN — DO NOT EDIT ----
//! Fixed-point math helpers used by spec-derived guards and properties.

#![allow(dead_code)]

/// Floor of `(a * b) / d`. Returns `0` if `d == 0` (caller must guard).
/// Uses saturating multiplication as a safe approximation; specs that need
/// exact u256-width fixed-point math should pin a checked widening crate
/// once the spec language exposes one.
#[inline]
pub fn mul_div_floor_u128(a: u128, b: u128, d: u128) -> u128 {
    if d == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    a.saturating_mul(b) / d
}

/// Ceiling of `(a * b) / d`. Same caveats as `mul_div_floor_u128`.
#[inline]
pub fn mul_div_ceil_u128(a: u128, b: u128, d: u128) -> u128 {
    if d == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let prod = a.saturating_mul(b);
    if prod % d == 0 {
        prod / d
    } else {
        (prod / d).saturating_add(1)
    }
}
/// Nearest `(a * b) / d`, with exact halves rounded upward.
#[inline]
pub fn mul_div_round_half_up_u128(a: u128, b: u128, d: u128) -> u128 {
    if d == 0 {
        return 0;
    }
    let prod = a.saturating_mul(b);
    let q = prod / d;
    let r = prod % d;
    let threshold = d / 2 + d % 2;
    if r >= threshold {
        q.saturating_add(1)
    } else {
        q
    }
}
// ---- END GENERATED ----
